lines.text: CL260223 - Amazing-Emu is live.
Dedicated Servers will need to be restarted to apply this hotfix.
This update removes the Photo Mode option from the in-game settings menu which was causing UI errors for users. It’ll be reinstated in a later update.
This briefing is for your eyes only, agent.
We're back! Another month, another update. Let's talk about everything coming your way. A new quest, new activities, Earth Magic and... Penguins?
Earth Magic
Finally - the fourth element has arrived. Earth Magic joins Air, Fire and Water, and brings a new, earthy flavour to Magic.
At level 14 Magic, you'll be able to equip Earth Runes for Staves and Wands. Earth attacks deal Blunt Damage, staggering enemies and interrupting attacks.

Earth Magic specialises in AOE Damage, launching waves of earth at the target. The final hit of the Staff Combo hits the area around the target too, catching nearby enemies. The Staff's Special Attack creates an earthquake, with multiple aftershocks. Charge it to increase the affected area. Once cast, you can leave it to do its thing while you reposition, to make terrain difficult for your foes.

There's also a defensive benefit to this - Armour of the Earth. Earth Magic hits build a defensive buff on you, reducing your damage taken. You can build up to 3 stacks, and they're consumed on your next incoming hit. You'll consume the stacks, and take less damage on that hit. Landing more hits keeps the stacks coming - so stay in the fight, push forward and maintain the stacks to reduce your damage. And, yes - At 60 Attack, you can enchant your melee weapons with this too, to build Armour of the Earth on-hit with melee as well.
Penguin Hunting

Ashenfall has been infiltrated by the Killer Gentoo Penguins - KGP for short - and we have received reports that over 200 of them have appeared across the continent of Ashenfall. It's time to get hunting. Penguins spawn in batches - no more than 3 agents at a time, per region. These reset at regular intervals of 7 in-game days so as you progress through your adventures, you'll spot more dotted around! Hidden in plain sight, these can be found, spotted and interacted with.

Once they flee, you'll collect a token - evidence they were here - leaving you a Penguin Coin. This coin will be used at a new shop in Bramblemead, with a Full Penguin Armour Set, KGP Hat, a Penguin Cape, and decorations for your base including new tapestries from iconic RuneScape Art Community founding member, and legend of the Forums:
Prezleek.

We've also added an amulet that improves chances to catch Pristine Fish, and a ring that reduces stamina for reeling in fish to make it easier to reel in the big one! These are the first steps we're making to improve fishing based on your feedback!
We'll be adding more rewards to the shop in the future so there'll be more to come back for, too!
A Reel Downer - New Quest

Over in Umbral Sands, someone’s having a rather difficult fishing trip. Head to the Manafem Clan’s camp for our new quest, A Reel Downer. Their fisherman’s catch won’t stop crying, and the clan can’t stand the taste of miserable fish.You’ll need to help him find a way to cheer them up. Apparently, happy fish taste better.

Finish the quest to unlock the Fishing Rod Rack recipe, giving your collection a proper display at home. You’ll also unlock trophy recipes for the sad fish, so if you catch a pristine one, you can mount it on your wall.
Nothing brightens up a home quite like a miserable fish.
The Rug Pull
There’s a new trail to uncover in Umbral Sands.
Four brothers stole a valuable carpet and some treasure from an ancient vault. But when the loot disappeared, greed and suspicion tore them apart.
None of the brothers survived, but they left behind their final journal entries, each telling their side of the story....
Find them scattered around the desert, piece together the clues and use the landmarks around you to work out where you need to dig.
Follow the trail to unlock plans for two new rugs for your base!
Letter Deliveries
If you’ve completed Letters from the Dead in Fellhollow, Postie Pete has some new delivery routes for you, taking you into Dowdun Reach and Umbral Sands.
Buy the plans for a regional post box using that region’s currency, then build it at your base. Each post box gives you letters for its own region, so you can choose where to make your rounds.
Deliveries in Dowdun Reach reward you with
Infernal Fragments
, which you can spend at Postie Pete’s
Evil Emporium
Over in Umbral Sands, you’ll earn
Garou Chits
to spend with the region’s merchants. Riches - or, a wage for your work, await!
PTR (Public Test Realm)
One suggestion we've heard a lot from players across our community spaces is something to the effect of "We'd love a PTR to help get hands on early and catch things if we can!"
We think that's a great idea, and we're taking our first steps towards making this happen!

We'll start with a select group of PC players who will explore upcoming builds, put the new features through their paces and help us identify issues that we may otherwise miss. This also lets us learn what works and what doesn't to make the PTR experience even better, if we are going to build it into a regular part of developing Dragonwilds.
What we want to be very transparent about a few things, though:

Due to the long lead times required for Console submission, any PTR on Steam is the build that is being deployed to consoles on release date. That means some of the issues discovered in the PTR before release would be resolved in a later patch.

Participation would also involve you backing up your saves and switching between a PTR branch and the Live version of the game. We'll provide instructions when the time comes, but it is crucial that you protect your progress when venturing across that Wilderness wall into the new branch!

We're going to test this out with a smaller, selected group initially to explore the branch, with dedicated spaces in Discord and Reddit to collate feedback - and contain spoilers. Our commitment in the wake of the PTR is that we will absolutely own, report and discuss what you discovered, what we're able to address, and what needs work. Diving into the PTR shouldn't just end with "Thanks for the feedback!" - we want it to feel like you know what happens next.
Bug Fixes
Fixed an issue where door opening animations looked smooth for the host but not for clients on that world.
Fixed an issue where Spell Books/ Spell Wheels would show the incorrect spells for the page when opened after using a lodestone or opening an interface.
Ascending Masterwork Armour now correctly increases its stats.
When filling stacks in chests, the stacks will now no longer pull from the Quick Access Bar.
Streamlined the process of interacting with Processing Stations to reduce the number of inputs.
Fixed an issue where Player-built structures on Dedicated Servers would lose collision and you would clip through them in certain circumstances.
Getting 99 Agility will now correctly trigger the achievement on consoles.
Fix for users who lost the ability to use the item wheel after using spell wheel hotkeys a few times.
Fixed an issue where summoning Sworn Servant "Buddy" would continually apply a Stamina Regen debuff even after despawning or expiring.
Added a new UI interface to showcase the number of enemies/waves attacking when a Base Raid event takes place.
Fixed an issue where clients in a hosted world would grow two trees from each planted seed.
Fix for the issue where the Quick Select wheel could not switch weapons during longer animations.
Fix for users who had adjusted their system clocks on PC being prevented from accessing Crossplay.
Deployed a fix where creating a new character using a renamed character's previous name would delete the original character.
Fix for Crafting Recipes that require six different materials that caused the UI to overflow into the quantity section.
Fixed an issue where users could use a broken 1-handed weapon by equipping a shield.
Resolved an issue where opening/closing the map would cause your inventory to stay open.
Resolved an issue where the Enchanted Weapon ambience has been tapped down.
Fixed an issue where Trunk Totem XP was multiplied incorrectly when various Trunk Totems were too close to each other.
Fix for High-Epic Graphics Settings displaying an incorrect LOD for a mountain in Umbral Sands.
Fix for an error message showing when disconnecting from the internet while logging in to Online play.
Resolved an issue where adding an item to your inventory would cause the inventory items to sort.
Resolved an Audio issue where Hosts would hear other players' Magic Wand SFX as if they were right next to them.
Fixed an issue where you could drag unrelated items into the fuel/combustible slot in the Campfire. Stop that.
Fix for a crash due to an audio reverb issue.
Fixed an issue where building menu icons looked pixelated.
Fixed a UI issue which caused the Compost Bins to display the incorrect status on use.
Fixed an issue where Gilded Gyrhawk, Glory, Strength, Magic and Salve Amulets were not calculating durability loss correctly with use.
Known Issues
Armour of the Earth Hit Reacts are not triggering their bespoke SFX.
If a player receives the same location twice in a row for Postbox Letter Delivery, the player must leave the area and return to complete the delivery.
In the Dowdun Reach area, the Camera unexpectedly pulls into the player model in certain spots.
Clients may appear as a default character for a brief time when first loading into a large world. Give it a minute and you'll pop right in as your normal self.
After being opened and then closed, doors will be slightly offset.
Using a mount appearance consumable without either base mount unlocked, will incorrectly show 'Mounts Unlocked'.
Pressing Up on the D-Pasd in the "Advanced" tab of Custom World Settings navigates up 5 menu entries, rather than the intended 1. Down on the D-Pad works fine!
These two in particular have been on our radar and we're introducing more telemetry tracking with 1.0.2 to help us better log data on these to investigate further:
Stuttering during auto-save following 1.0.1 update
In some instances, only one client will be able to join an Xbox-hosted world.
And that’s JUST this month’s update! Next month, we’ll have…
Luminance
This December, Elves arrive in Ashenfall with the Luminance Update, bringing a new adventure, the musical magic of the Lyre and a new way to build and shape your journey across Ashenfall.

You'll be exploring a new outpost area that will emerge from the fog on the edges of Ashenfall, meet new characters and learn to pluck, strum or otherwise noodle on a Lyre to resonate with songstones to progress! A continent wide hunt for a sinister Bounty Hunter will net you valuable resources and a way to earn Harmonised Crystal Fragments - valuable currency if you're in the market for new Elven gear. (You are, by the way.)
Embrace the Elven fantasy with a new Prifddinas-inspired building kit, a range of new character customisation options and craftable Elven armour and Weapons!

And what's a RuneScape adventure without another skill to level? Prayer joins Dragonwilds this December! Call upon Saradomin to smite your foes, Guthix to keep you and your friends in the fight, or Zamorak to trade a little health for some serious extra damage. Just remember, the gods all have their own ideas about how you should survive Ashenfall.
All of this lays the foundations and weaves in the first threads of our most ambitious, exciting questline yet in the Blood Crystal Saga. There's still dragons involved, of course.
Alongside all of this, we're continuing to improve the core experience with quality-of-life changes across platforms and targeted visual improvements for Nintendo Switch 2.
For now, that’s all we’ve got - but we’ll be in touch again soon. Until next time, have fun out there, adventurers. Be good, and we’ll see you in Ashenfall!

lines.text: Hello adventurers! Here's what's in our latest patch.

Thanks for your patience with us on this one. We'll be in touch very soon with the latest updates on all things 1.0.2 and what's to come next month! Until then, be good, and we'll see you in Ashenfall.
Here's what's on our radar in regards to known issues.
We're looking to deploy a hotfix as soon as possible to address the following:

Users are unable to skip the "Corrupted Save" warning popup on the main menu on controller in some circumstances. Some users have reported that repeatedly hitting "accept"/"A"/"X" on controller or disconnecting and reconnecting the controller skips this, but we're working on a holistic fix.

Here's what we're aware of beyond tomorrow's hotfix - we'll get these resolved as soon as possible.

The other Air Stave attacks work as intended as do Wands - there are also the other elemental types and melee and ranged, of course, but we know you want to live our your Mage fantasy. We've got you.

Fixes for skips in the Scorned Wilderness Raid.
Fix for an menu navigation error when PS5 users sign out of their account while accepting an invite.
A fix for XBOX Series X hosted worlds where only one user can join at a time.
Fix for inventory not persisting when switching worlds.
Mucksplosion is not correctly affecting the 3x3 radius it shows before casting.
An issue where some Corrupted World Saves are disappearing for players.
Fix for users experiencing a failed download initiation on Jagex Launcher.

posts.title: Our 1.0.1 update is now live! | Eye on Ashenfall

lines.text: Save Fixes

The big headline for this one is a range of fixes targeting the disappearing world saves we've seen reported, as well as a catch-up mechanic for corrupted character saves that will let you drop in with aggregated stats and Tier 4 gear to get you back in the fight. Hop in and give those a try, but we're aware there may still be the occasional player affected by other, extraneous instances of save issues that we're still collecting data on. We're talking about very, very small numbers of affected players, but it matters all the same. Beyond that, let's get into what else is coming in 1.0.1.
1.0.1 and Core Improvements
What goes up...
Introducing... the Jump Attack. It does exactly what you think it does.
Unlock the Skill Tree perk "Death From Above!"
Any time you are
slightly

above the max height of the double jump's arc from the ground, inputting an attack will plunge you downward to slam into unfortunate victims below. Damage scales with the weapon you have equipped, so make sure you're holding something hefty before you leap. And yes, Windstep counts here. What goes up, must come crashing down.
I've Got Shooters
Added the Ranged skill perk - Ammo Recovery, and it's Greater version later in the Skill Tree - Greater Ammo Recovery.
Adds a chance to recover arrows from the bodies of slain enemies.
Ranged weapon subclasses are receiving their own special attack variants to make them feel more aligned with the fantasy of using the Shortbow, Longbow or Crossbow.
Shortbow: Rapid Fire - Hop backwards and fire off three arrows in quick succession. The target can be switched between this volley of shots to spread the damage.
Longbow: Power Shot - take a knee to draw an arrow at full strength. Let fly to loose a staggering, enormously powerful shot at great distance.
Crossbow: Heavy Bolt - rack a bolt and let it fly after a short charge. Hits like Asgarnian Ale on an empty stomach, and applies Enchanted effects on-hit.

Introduced the Low Blow Skill Perk: Ranged attacks that hit the enemy in the legs (lower third of the body or their legs) applies "Hamstrung" which reduces enemy movement speed for a short while. Tiny and Colossal Enemies are immune.
...And The Rest
Increased inventory space from 32 to 40.
Added a toggle for the Visceral Attack Camera change.
[img src="][/img]
Fixed an issue where users on mounts could not open the map correctly.
Obstacles and Enemies now respawn in the Scorned Wildnerness Raid on reset/next run-through.
Reduced aggro range for enemies across the game to prevent forming a bit of a follow-train like a Fally Drop Party.
Enemy mob respawn timers extended so they stay dead for longer as you clear areas.
Fixed an issue where users on controller were unable to sort chests with L3/LS correctly.
Polish pass on Mining nodes across the world to ensure they're all above ground and can be mined.
Goblin "barks" (ambient noises they make) should now sound less like they've just seen you and are yelling.
Improvements on the Sort functionality - Weight, Type and Latest.
Weight: Cumulative Stack Weight, Heaviest First.
Type: Categories of item, alphabetically.
Latest: The most recently picked up items first.
Adding a dedicated Ring AND Amulet slot.
Thanks to Thurnax, NeganTWD, Cloud_N0ne and others who suggested this.
The Amulet of Glory was providing additional bonuses above what was initially intended, so we're tapping those numbers back down to better align with what we wanted it to be.
We're adding the Ultra Compost Bin - because "Super" just wasn't cutting it anymore.
Adding the Large Compost Bucket, which has a larger capacity.
Now stop asking.
Adding a Completed Quests tab including a short summary of the outcome of the quest.
[img src="][/img]
Overdrive can now be cast on the Advanced Spinning Wheel.
Rune Arrows and Bolts now do more damage than Adamant. 4.9x versus 4.2x.
The Fishing Cape now correctly displays the Skillcape Perk - You have a small chance to instantly catch a fish.
Removed the ability to rebind keybinds for settings that could soft lock the player in certain instances:
Interaction
Remove Spell
Building
Cancel Building
Quick Interact
Crafting
Crafting Tab Left/Right
Quest Dialogue
Continue Conversation
Cancel Conversation
Select Answer 1/2/3/4
Additional Bug Fixes
Fixed an issue where users could clip through the floor when teleporting to Cataclysm Keep from Commander Zilyana.
Resolved an issue where PS5 users were unable to see the assigned Sort button on chests.

Resolved an issue where Players who had acquired Quest Items early (through multiplayer sessions) would be unable to progress to the next region. E.g. Imaru's Head prevented the player from entering Fellhollow, etc.
Resolved an issue where users could crash when selecting Online play while being Offline.
Fixed an issue where Rain would cause visual effects to be visible inside player housing at any graphical setting. It no longer rains indoors!
Resolved an issue where Sanguine Urns within the radius of the Scorned Wilderness were not displaying correctly.
Resolved an issue where the Skills Page description states Magic Focus can be crafted at the Crafting Table instead of the Blacksmith's Bench.
Fixed an issue where images in the Journal could scale incorrectly. Begone, giant Bandos symbol!
Fixed an issue where Hosts would unlock achivements triggered by a player in the world.
Resolved a bug causing Ascension Cores to not drop from Kuldra in some circumstances.
Fixed an issue where users with Emojis in their name on PC would not be able to join PS5 or XBOX player hosted worlds.
Fixed the Dragon Med Helm icon to be the right shade of red. So, so sorry.
All platforms can now access the UI Scaling option as intended.
Special Attacks from Ranged will now trigger gamepad vibration as intended.

Fixed an issue where ores would respawn instantly when teleporting in the Scorned Wilderness raid. Nice try.

Our commitment to you is clear: Dragonwilds is the third pillar of the RuneScape series, and one we will continue to support throughout the years to come. posts.title: Our 1.0 Check-In Survey is now Live!

lines.text: Hello adventurers! While we're continuing our work on the updates for 1.0 and while the patch for 1.0.0.7 is being processed on platforms, we're back with our regularly scheduled Check-in Survey! The survey will be available until
7AM GMT on the 8th October 2026.
As always, if you're encountering bugs, head to the Bug Reports in our Official Discord.
Click here to complete the Survey!
Epic Games Store players are now back online and can enjoy Crossplay again!
Resolved an issue where users could quit the Edit Appearance menu before the Character Save had completed.
This is a preventative measure - work towards currently affected "corrupted" saves is still ongoing.
We'll share an update later today.
Resolved an issue on PC where incorrect filenames would be accepted as Character files.
Some corrupted World Saves were no longer visible in the menu for players.

For some users, this save may also let you rejoin the world - but we are not considering this a comprehensive fix. Some users may still not be able to access their world after this fix, but the visibility of the world in the list was the core target of this step in our process.
Fixed an issue where some  users would crash when selecting "Online" play while being offline.
Hello adventurers!
We’re targeting this hotfix to go live on Friday.
We’re sharing the notes with you
today
so you’re aware of where we’re at, and we’ll be submitting it the consoles with the expectation that this verification
will take several days
This is based on your feedback around the updates knocking crossplay offline – we hear you, and we’re trying to avoid a weekend of disrupted gameplay for Nintendo Switch 2 players.
The big topic of conversation is: we’re investigating the fixes about Save Corruption – world and character. We’re testing methods that will,
hopefully
, restore your missing saves. We need longer to investigate these solutions and the potential recovery options.
We’re removing the
most common cause
, to mitigate impact for further people:
the Edit Appearance button is going to disappear until we’ve resolved the issue.

Restoring some saves has meant that the world has been reset to default settings – which means that Custom or Creative worlds will have been reverted to Normal worlds. These might be in your Normal save lists!
Here’s what we’re targeting a fix with 1.0.0.5 on Friday:
Users no longer fail to connect to Multiplayer servers with more than 2 players present
This also specifically resolves multiplayer clients on XBOX being unable to connect if 2 users are already in the world.
AI will now respawn as intended on starting the second Scorned Wilderness Raid attempt.
Fixing an issue where joining a modded Dedicated Server from consoles would corrupt a player save.

lines.text: Today marks the start of our next journey. Thank you to the millions (yes, millions!) of you who joined us during Early Access. We're now live on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, XBOX Series X | S and PC on Epic Games Store, Jagex Launcher and Steam.
Our Early Access Journey

In April 2025 we launched into Early Access with the first Dragon General, Velgar, and the first two regions: Brynmoor and Ghornfell. We launched with 9 unique skills to level up, unlocking powerful, transformative Skill Spells to make the mundanity of survival a little more magical – no more grinding through countless trees, chopping until the sun comes up. 12 Unique armour sets, across 3 combat styles, supported by a range of weapons up to Iron tier.

In June 2025 we expanded our Magic Skill Tree, added additional building pieces including the Palisade Walls for protecting against Base Raids (which we’ve rebalanced and tuned down based on player feedback).

In September we added Ranged skill tree abilities including Hunter Sense, Spectral Arrow and and Snare Skill Spells. We also added poison, barbed and flaming arrows to deal poison, bleed and fire damage, as well as enchanted bolts for Crossbows (including the iconic Blurite Crossbow). We also added the Custom and Creative world options with over 50 custom world setting variables for you to make your world, your way, and tens of thousands of creative and custom worlds have been made since then!

In December, our first Major Update “Fellhollow” arrived with the Farming skill, a new building kit, two new NPCs and a shop for trading Soul Fragments with Death himself. Material upgrades brought you the Castle kit to make a spooky stronghold. You can also earn and equip Steel tier gear, complete with its iconic plumed Full Helm, and then made RuneScape history by adding Mounts! Ride a terrorbird and traverse the treacherous terrain in style! The second Dragon boss, Imaru the Revenant Dragon has tested, and will continue to test, the strength of your soul and offers unique rewards for those who grant her finality and peace.
[img src="https://framerusercontent.com/images/WICbTehr0q1lflHrMx61etRt1wY.png" style="aspect-ratio: 1920 / 1080;"][/img]

We added more to Fellhollow with our minor updates, monthly content drops adding quests, rewards and new decorations – new repeatable content in the form of Spectral Platforming, Buried Treasures and Letters for the Dead, and quests in the form of “Things That Go Boom In The Night”, “Doric’s Quest”, “Letters for the Dead”, “What Remains is Written” and “Mirror, Mirror”.

In March, we launched our next Major Update, with 4 more quests for players to take on, a new boss to overcome in the legendary Black Knight Titan, and a new region – Dowdun Reach. We launched support for Dedicated Servers, improved controller support, and a ton of bug fixes, before the arrival of Fishing.
[img src="https://framerusercontent.com/images/H8ZOS9RD779fd3yFCfLETgcGw9w.png" style="aspect-ratio: 1920 / 1080;"][/img]

We added three new quests: “Cook’s Assistant”, “Animal Magnetism” and “A Room with a Garou” alongside the Fishing skill which let you catch pristine fish to make new wall-mounted decorative trophies of your finest catches, providing the best healing-per-stack of any food item. We added Auto-run, auto-magnetising nearby items in the world to reduce inputs picking up items around you, the option to hide your helmet to show off your beautiful face and stopped Chickens, Cows and Kebbits from automatically attacking the player unprovoked so you can enjoy your cozy abode or a chill walk around in peace.
[img src="https://framerusercontent.com/images/OccuPZdkqacJER4niXWnWhq39E.png" style="aspect-ratio: 1920 / 1080;"][/img]

We reworked health and healing to let you tick-eat food like the other RuneScape games for optimal survivability in combat. We removed Wardstone to make your health bar more clearly representing your survivability, but also adding Sanguine Urns around the world to increase your Max HP by 10, permanently, for each unique one you find and use.

Our latest and largest Major Update, Umbral Sands, introduced a new form of Mount – the flying carpet – and introduced you to a region inspired by the Kharidian Deserts of RuneScape. Within this region, we introduced the Kalphite Queen and her brood, Fuzan the Fire Dragon and the Kot’Haar, sentient golems of Obsidian, given life by an Elder Artefact. We also added the Nightmare Crucible, allowing you to earn upgrade materials to power up your favourite weapons from lower Power Levels to be max level to face Kuldra with the release of Scorned Wilderness.  The region allows users to craft Adamant Armour, Red Dragonhide and Infinity Robes as well as additional vestiges including Obsidian Armour, the Obsidian shield and the Fire Cape. We expanded the Skill Trees for Mining and Woodcutting, giving you new Skill Spells and passive rewards, and added more NPC traders for users to trade with.
[img src="https://framerusercontent.com/images/SKDl2hlRvRZIC3eGFpDbGUpG4.jpg" style="aspect-ratio: 3840 / 2160;"][/img]
What's New in 1.0?
New Content
Added support for Consoles! This includes PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, XBOX Series X | S and PC on Epic Games Store, Jagex Launcher and Steam.
Added Crossplay!
In the in-game menu, worlds can now be enabled as crossplay when you load them.
Crossplay worlds will be shown in the world browser.
Players now have the option to make their worlds crossplay or not each time they host a multiplayer world
Dedicated servers now also have crossplay option.
You can now join worlds through invite codes! Invite codes can be entered in the world browser screen, and are shown in the in game pause menu.
Added the Scorned Wilderness quest:
Regicide.

Added the Scorned Wilderness region. This area includes "The Hub" which is a new area which players can build in, and the Raid area which does not permit building, because of the big dragon. Speaking of which...
Added new end-game boss, Kuldra, the God-Eater!
Big Momma herself.
Don't actually call her that.
Added a new enemy type: Goblin Thug
Added a new enemy type: Goblin Poisonshot Archer
Added a new enemy type: Garou Exile
Added a new enemy type: Garou Lightning Berserker

Added a new enemy type: Blazing Black Knight

Added a new enemy type: Black Dragons
We've got plenty of new gear for you to get stuck into, too.

The Dragon Scimmy is real, chat!

Killing Kuldra will ensure you get a drop - the Dragon Kiteshield, and then a Cape to wear with pride. In a slight deviation from previous iterations, this shield won't be a Dragonfire shield as you had in previous Dragon Generals.
There is also going to be a selection of pieces of the
iconic
Dragon armour - glorious, resplendent and
red,
including the
Dragon Scimitar
and the
Dragon Crossbow.
These are earned through repeat adventures into the Scorned Wilderness - provided you're successful again.
Added the Advanced Spinning Wheel
Once unlocked, this will be a new processing bench in the build menu, separate from the Spinning Wheel.
Items that can be processed in the regular Spinning Wheel cannot be used in the Advanced Spinning Wheel.
Here's all the new items you'll be collecting:
Runite Ore - requires Adamant Pickaxe or greater
Luminite Ore - requires Adamant Pickaxe or greater

Black Dragon Hide - crafted at the Advanced Tannery

Draconic Vis Wax - crafted at the Brewing Cauldron.
Vis Cloth - crafted at the Loom using Vis Fibers and Draconic Vis Wax.
Magic Tree Seeds are coming with 1.0.1 to allow you to grow your own!
We've added a new magic weapon type... Wands!

Wands are a more mobile, fast-paced way to deal more damage at a comparatively lower damage output. These will still apply buildup of knockdowns, burns and slows that you expect from Air, Fire and Water magic. You'll be able to use wands to move more fluidly in combat and get around, but also hang back with a Staff and lay down more damage if you want!
Attack
Added
Sprint Attacks
- Unlocks the ability to perform a unique Sprint Attack after sprinting for a short distance.
Added the
Enchant Weapon: Water Skill Spell
. Enchant your current Melee weapon with the power of Water! Strike enemies with Water damage and occasionally create healing orbs to restore your health. 15x Water + 5x Astral Runes (300s Cooldown)
Added the
Tempest Shield Upgrade
- increasing the duration of the Spell.
Enchant Weapon
spells have had their durations increased to 5 minutes.

's base cooldown has been reduced to 45 seconds.
Ranged
At level 60 - increased chance for Enchanted Crossbow Bolts to trigger their effects on-hit.

's cooldown has been reduced to 45 seconds.
Ranged is firmly in our sights to get some extra attention in coming updates between now and the release of Luminance this winter, so stay tuned for more to come on that.
Magic
Added
Runic Refund
- Grants a 30% chance to preserve your runes when attacking with magic.
Added
Enfeeble
- Weakens the Attacks of the targeted opponent. 20x Astral + 20x Water Runes. (75s Cooldown)
Added
Vengeance
- Is being vindictive a virtue? I think so! A spell that reflects your enemies' damage right back at them. 20x Astral + 10x Earth Runes (60s Cooldown)
Mining
We've previously added the
Ore & Stone Storage
- Unlocks the Ore and Stone Storage, a high capacity storage for ores and stones.
They said I couldn't make a Rock and Stone reference here.
Added

- Drop 5 ore on the ground and turn it into a personal mining vein. 100x Earth Rune + 100x Nature Rune (1500s Cooldown)
Added

In case you missed this in our previous update, we added the

Wood Weight Reduction
has been moved to Level 88 - reduces the weight of wood by 50%.
Added the

- now it conjures THREE spectral axes, carving through even more trees along their path in a cone in front of you.
Construction
Added the Eye of Oculus Upgrade - When destroying pieces using Eye of Oculus, the eye now magnetises the recycled material into the players inventory.
Added New building pieces: Pets - starting with Perches for Birds.
Artisan
Added the
Storage Ledger

- interact with this, and any items in your inventory that have an existing stack in any linked chest will auto-sort and be filed away correctly. Previously after a expedition you have to run around your entire base or storeroom interacting/filling stacks on every chest to unload your stuff.... now, you just walk up to the ledger and drop everything off at once.
Added
Overdrive
- a long requested Skill Spell. Cast on mechanical-based processing stations to empower them and boost their processing speed for a while. It's superheat, for things that aren't super hot.
Moved

to level 56. We've tapped down the base version of this spell's effectiveness at restoring durability to encourage using repair benches where possible, but to still make Magical Mending work in a pinch.
Added
Superheat Upgrade
- increasing the duration of Superheat.
Added
Overdrive Upgrade
- increasing the duration of Overdrive.
Added
Magical Mending Upgrade
- increased radius and durability restoration. This puts the spell slightly above where it currently sits, but feels more earned.
Runecrafting
Added the
Home Teleport
spell - Teleport safely back to your claimed bed and enjoy a peaceful, undisturbed night's sleep. 15x Law Runes (900s Cooldown).
Yes, at last.
Gameplay Changes

We've made significant changes to the building system! Huge builds that would previously take minutes(!!!) to load will load much faster now. So now, finally, no more long waits when teleporting back to your base! It's a new system, so if you do encounter any issues please let the team know and we'll gladly investigate!
We've improved LODs across the game world, and we're targeting yet another fix for these with the 1.0.1 update in October, too.
We've made a bunch of changes to how you move and behave in combat. These changes are broad and far-reaching, but the connecting thread across it all is that it was driven by your feedback.
The Primary Attack button on controller will now be R1/RB/R - special attacks are now on R2/RT/ZR.

Let's talk camera: from the outset, we've had the camera connected very closely to the player. Your movements never strayed too far from your center of the screen. We've added a "deadzone" where you're able to freely roam the middle third of the screen before the camera starts to follow you. This lets you sprint across the world with a little more freedom in your movement and evade in combat without the camera going rogue. This should also help with Agility courses, if you're looking to do your laps.
Parrying will now restore 50% of your max stamina allowing you to quickly turn the tide with a burst of energy if you time it correctly - increasing the risk/reward of timing it just right.

The camera and parry also allow you to pull off "Visceral Attacks" - a follow-up attack that you can do when you successfully parry and enemy. The attack is optional - you can dodge, make a run for it or even throw in a Weapon Special Attack instead in that moment. Speaking of Special Attacks...
Special Attacks will now consume a portion of the player's
Special Attack Bar
This allows us to buff these attacks and reduce their stamina costs so that they can be more powerful now that we can limit the frequency of these attacks.
Your special attack bar will slowly recharge over time meaning players will want to ensure they time their attacks well to get the most out of their limited special attack potential!

You will be able to use them less often, but they will feel more powerful with each use. Things like the Titan's Wrath and the Greatsword Special will hit harder, and be more of an active ability choice.

Sprint attacks have been added to the game, allowing you to open with a big strike once you've levelled up your Attack skill a little. You'll be able to open a combo with a strong hit - but that's not all...
You'll be able to cancel attacks, gathering and spell-casting actions with dodging and blocking.

This means you can opt out of those pesky wind-ups or spells you've committed to mid-combat. But if you don't want to cancel the spell - you can now move while casting a range of spells, including Enchant Weapon, Windstep and Surge as just a few examples. Use that new-found window of opportunity to buff yourself, catch a breath and dive back in to the fray.

The Skill Spell wheel now has 4 hotkeys that let you auto-cast the first four choices in the Radial Menu. These are mapped to the triggers, allowing you to open the wheel and instantly trigger the respective spell.
Remember to use the Spellbook in the menu to re-order these spells to fit your muscle memory! Rocksplosion, my beloved,
We're also still investigating how we can introduce a dedicated quick-cast button for a particular spell or item in a future update.

The "Feather Fall" special ability has been removed from the Leggings of Lightness, for balance and maintenance reasons. We replaced it with an ability that makes Windstep cost zero runes to cast while the Leggings are equipped. The Leggings still also grant extra carry weight capacity as before.
In case you missed it in 0.12.1 - Ammunition can now be swapped on the D-Pad or Scroll Wheel. Flip between Runes or Arrow Types depending on your equipped weapon.
The Abyssal Whip now requires a recipe found in the Umbral Sands to complete to unlock its Masterwork Weapon potential. In the interim, you'll be able to craft the
Abysmal Whip (PL4)
as an intermediary weapon which will not have the Special Attack, with a marginal tap-down in damage. Upgrading to the Masterwork Abyssal Whip elevates the weapon to
PL7.
Due to overwhelming demand, Ava'a Accumulator no longer makes sound when equipped. Shut the cluck up.

With the launch on Consoles, some Smart TVs may attempt to hard-force Game/HDR picture settings within the TV itself. For some users, this may seem to be extra bloom-y or brighter than expected. We'd encourage users to check their TV's Picture Settings and lower the following three settings to suit your preferences:
Contrast
Colour
and, if applicable - Contrast Enhancer.
We rolled out a range of fixes for navigation through menu systems and crafting stations, both for Controller and Keyboard and Mouse.
Tooltips can now be scrolled through.
The Quest Menu sidebar can be collapsed to view the Map fully.
Active Lodestones are now visible on the map, not just the lodestone menu.
Map icons now grow in size when hovered over.
Map icons now have a small tooltip when hovered.

Moderation was added too! You can now report problematic worlds, rude players, griefers and hackers. Reports are fully moderated by real human beings - no AI involved - and can lead to temporary world and player bans.
We've tweaked the damage of the Dire Wolves and Garou of Ghornfell to be marginally less terrifying, while you're trying to establish a foothold in the second area.
Dig your heels in and fight them!
Bug Fixes

With launch we'll be sharing a Known Issues live page that we'll be updating throughout the week with Vital Information of issues we're tracking! But, just as a cool statistic - in the process of securing our 1.0 build, going gold and launching onto consoles, the team found, logged and fixed 2,665 bugs. Two thousand, six hundred and sixty five. Yep! So many of these you'll never see, wooshed away - like magic!
For now, here's what Community-driven fixes we're deploying today.
Fix to Fuzan occasionally getting stuck at 0hp in the Fight Caves and fail to respawn.
Ranged ammo drops from will once again magnetize to the player as intended.
The Nightmare Crucible did not end correctly when completed if the player had summoned a Buddy.
The Red Desert Cape Vestige is now correctly included in the Drop Table.
Fix for users who encountered a blocker when interacting with Chests, particularly in Dowdun Reach, that didn't work when interacted with on another player's world.
Fixed an issue where Tree Canopies would not disappear when the tree was felled.
Adjustments to reduce the probability of trees failing to topple when felled.
Building over cliff edges no longer causes the player to be met with rapidly changing weather.
Single axe swings will no longer be able to both split a tree and remove the stump, to avoid accidental stump removals!
Decorative Gems are now able to be placed on Foundations and Flooring.
Players on mounts can now eat or drink from the hot bar as well as the inventory.
Resolved an issue where dying to the Kalphite Queen in certain circumstances would cause the Gravestone to be stuck in the arena, instead of spawning outside the entrance.
The Water Barrel, Rain Catcher and Compost Bin's "Hold to Delete" button has been reverted to a one-tap delete.
Fixed Kothaar and Kalphite damage values to scale correctly with the Hard Mode Difficulty option.
Resolved an issue affecting the Trunk Totems leaving some unable to be destroyed.
The Roof on the Yew Farming Plots no longer blocks the Humidify Skill Spell from reaching other plots.
Watermelon Jerky's maximum stack value has been raised from 50 to 99.
The Bow of Elidinis can no longer use Bleed, Poison and Fire Arrows.
Watch This Space

From today, until the 4th October, you can earn yourself the Dragonwilds Twitch Badge! Tune in to your favourite streamer and watch 30 minutes of RuneScape: Dragonwilds to earn yourself a badge for your Twitch account to wear with pride!

This is not the end of RuneScape: Dragonwilds. A new chapter begins with this release, and the start of an ambitious, multi-year journey into Ashenfall and its secrets. This winter, we'll be shipping Luminance, our next Content Update which will bring a new building kit, and so much more alongside it. And as for changes to combat on the horizon? Well, let's just say... Magic
rocks
. Literally.
[img src="][/img]
You know the usual - follow our socials (Twitter, BSky, Instagram, Facebook, Twitch, YouTube and TikTok!) and get involved with Reddit and join the Discord.

As always, we love seeing your comments and feedback, and we're very excited to see you taking on everything Ashenfall has to offer. Thank you for being part of this historic moment in RuneScape's history. We cannot wait to share more with you soon.

posts.title: Dragonwilds Is Leaving Early Access. Our Price Isn't.

lines.text: Since we launched into Early Access, we've been extremely proud of the amazing work that has gone into RuneScape: Dragonwilds. So many of you have taken the plunge into Ashenfall, and with every update we are humbled by the number of you trying out Dragonwilds, recommending it to friends and leaving reviews on Steam. The feedback has been incredible, and the game continues to improve with every update, guided and informed by our vision, and your feedback, working together in harmony.
RuneScape: Dragonwilds is not stopping at our 1.0 release, and we will continue to deliver monthly updates to you as the game grows.
The game, containing the entirety of Kuldra's Saga and the Free Updates around it,
is staying the same price once 1.0 releases

Dragonwilds' success is because of the invaluable participation of our Early Access players, but also thanks to the support and excitement shared by the countless number of fans waiting for Kuldra's Saga to be complete before you took the plunge with us. We hope this small gesture goes some way to showing our endless appreciation for your support and belief.
We'll also be launching our next Update in the coming Winter - one we're naming
Luminance

. This, much like the minor updates, is free, too. We'll share more about our 2027 plans once we've delivered our 1.0 release, and you can tune into our Summit at RuneFest on October 3rd, to hear more about 2027 and the next Saga in Ashenfall's story.

posts.title: Kuldra's Saga - An Update From Mod Dutch

lines.text: Hello Adventurers!
It is I, Mod Dutch, come to you with a message about the future of Dragonwilds. Hold on, sheath that sword, ease your bowstring and pause casting that water spell, I assure you, it is good news!
TL;DR: Our 1.0 release on September 15th is not the end of Dragonwilds. Far from it.

Ever since it became clear that there was high enthusiasm for a survival game set in the RuneScape franchise, we’ve been diligently planning (oftentimes cackling with glee) what comes next. Mod Rook, our intrepid Creative Director, together with Mod Raven, envisioned a satisfying wrap-up to the story of the Dragon Queen Kuldra to coincide with our game exiting Early Access, so that RuneScape and survival fans who had been holding off until this point, could experience the complete story from beginning to end.

At Jagex we look at our RuneScape titles as ongoing projects, always. They are never done, because they continuously evolve. That has been the way for twenty-five years of adventuring on Gielinor. Changes, fixes, overhauls, new content, amazing new sagas, new raids, new bosses, new quest areas – it’s a continuous flow of updates, informed by the players’ opinions and feedback. This is deeply ingrained in the DNA of Jagex.

Recall

"She is here: the pinnacle of dragon creation, the queen, fused with divine blood and now housing the elemental power of my kin." - Rasthin
Hello adventurers!

Our road to the end of Kuldra's Saga is clear. Our 0.12.1 update will be the last stop before we put you face to face with the God-Eater herself. Darkness gathers. Wild magic storms overhead. The only way out is through.

We're going to be sharing a full breakdown of Agility, as well as a Dev Diary condensing 0.12.1's features very soon ahead of it's release at the end of this month. Firstly though, let's talk about Scorned Wilderness.
[img src="][/img]

Until now, we've shipped Major Updates that are expansive continents that add a new region, rich with resources, quests, secrets and lore for you to explore at your own pace. These expansion-like updates have grown the world and set the stage for the adventures you'll be undertaking within it. Scorned Wilderness is
not
like these updates. Scorned Wilderness represents the culmination of our learnings from everything we've built within RuneScape: Dragonwilds so far - but it is
not

the end. Our journey is only beginning, and we're excited to share more about what's coming after Scorned Wilderness once we launch it. Rest assured, our intentions are the same as they always have been - to keep delivering more of the game you love, at a pace that delights and excites you.

We've referred to it so far as a "Raid" because we know that for those of you chasing Twisted Bows, ending up at the toothy end of Zebak, or who've earned the scars from the Liberation of Mazcab, RuneScape Raids
mean
something. We agree.

For those of you unfamiliar with RuneScape raids, we've got you. A Raid is typically a high-end challenge pitched against a player, or groups. You'll be subjected to a gauntlet, delving into a dungeon, raiding a tomb, or... say... charging into an Anima storm to take down a God-Eater. We're the latter. A raid includes unique mechanics or combat challenges testing your mettle and survival skills to hold out against onslaughts of enemies as you fight for a foothold and every inch of ground gained is a victory in itself. Ultimately, you'll rise to the challenge and earn the right to challenge the boss.
Our first
Raid

pits you (and your cadre of adventurer allies, if you so wish) against a landscape that was ripped apart by wild anima, and the fury of Black Dragons. You will traverse across floating islands, fighting through attacks by the God-Eater herself to reach her. Each of her tyrannical, terrible heads channels the fury of Gielinor's dragons - but she is more than the sum of her parts. Those of you who have slain countless Dragons on the Gielinor mainland will recognise some of her attacks. She shares heritage with other Dragonkin experiments,
but she is more
[img src="][/img]

Beyond Kuldra, you'll be able to harvest resources to craft Ancestral Robes, Black Dragonhide gear and of course, Rune Armour. Claim your rewards for a dragon-slaying job well done, and you'll be able to gear yourself up with some new kit that will let you roam the entirety of Ashenfall in relative safety and security. For now, anyway...

Killing Kuldra will ensure you get the latest version of the Dragon Shield as you've come to expect with the previous Dragons, and then a Cape to wear with pride. There is also going to be a selection of pieces of the
iconic
Dragon armour - glorious, resplendent and
red,
including the
Dragon Scimitar
and the
Dragon Crossbow.
There's a few extra secret goodies on that RDT (that's a Rare Drop Table to you and me) that we're not spoiling yet - you'll have to slay that Dragon and get spooned to find them out.

We're excited to keep working on finishing up what is undoubtedly our most vertical, most anima-warped update to date. We're really excited to get it into your hands, and for you to be able to enjoy the entire RuneScape: Dragonwilds experience so far with new combat, new movement, and so much more. With that in mind, while we've aimed to share things early, give you sneak peeks and even some deep dives in things like blog posts, we're going to be making a conscious choice NOT to spoil the Raid.

We'll be sharing more about our work towards the release, including our process for finding and fixing bugs, and the changes we're delivering to change combat and movement from minute one, but the Raid is something else entirely.

It's going to be something you can only experience for the first time once, so we want it to be totally new, and completely engrossing. We hope you can understand, and we're excited to see you taking on the God-Eater when it launches on September 15th.
- The RuneScape: Dragonwilds Team

lines.text: We're making combat less clunky - here's a look at what's coming in our next few updates.

For a long time, we've been listening to feedback around combat - your steam reviews, your comments on Reddit and Discord, and replies on our socials, everywhere! We went back and forth, chatting to hundreds of you, combing through thousands of survey responses, and gathering info. One word kept coming up - clunky! Clunky clunky clunky.
We've boiled it down to some core principles. Here's what we want to address:
Blocking doesn't clearly or consistently reduce damage as expected.
Stamina management is a challenge.
You want to quick-switch and quick-cast more fluidly.
Switching ammo types in combat is punishing.
Weapon Specs should feel stronger, and more impactful to use.
You can't move while casting skill spells.
You want to really punish enemies for parrying them.
Fall damage hurts.
Right - let's fix that. Enter: The
Core Improvements Team.

We're making good progress on improving performance, additional ambient VFX and tons of optimisation for Fog, trees, grass and even the coastline. All of that is intended to make the experience more stable/smooth for you to focus on what you do best. Smacking the living daylights out of goblins.

We're also adding more to the existing jump to improve its "ledge forgiveness" - as in, if you walk off a ledge, there's a small window of time for you to jump before you cartoonishly plummet to your demise. There's more to come with agility, but we'll speak to that separately.

Camera-relative aiming will become the default controller input.
Where your camera is looking will be where your attacks and spells will go.

The Old School RuneScape classic, the Special Attack bar, is also coming to Dragonwilds.

Players familiar with RuneScape will be familiar with how this will work already, but as of 1.0, Special Attacks will consume a portion of the player's special attack bar. This allows us to strengthen some of these attacks and reduce their stamina costs so that they can be more powerful now that we can limit the frequency of these attacks. Your special attack bar will slowly recharge over time meaning players will want to ensure they time their attacks well to get the most out of their limited special attack potential! You will be able to use them less often, but they will feel more powerful with each use. They'll feel less like "another move", and more like a conscious decision to use a Special Ability.

These will still apply buildup of knockdowns, burns and slows that you expect from Air, Fire and Water magic. In our first sneak peek at Umbral Sands, a lot of you rightly noticed a player casting a new kind of spell - Water Magic! Since we launched into Early Access and since we built out the Magic Skill Tree, we heard your feedback around wanting additional magic types, and Water was a natural fit for us.
Here's Mod Pointy, Lead Designer to talk about how Water Magic is going to work in combat:

We knew Water Magic was going to be next up as soon as we looked at the Magic Skill and where we wanted it to go. It's a natural progression and it's also how our RuneScape veterans expect progression to go. With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at our magic styles and what they offered. We've got special attacks from Staves like the Zamorak Staff, and the core identities of Fire and Air magic are pretty clear, too. Fire magic deals widespread damage and burning enemies continually tick down, while Air magic is targeted, but combos and special attacks can floor most lower-level enemies and keep them controlled at a distance.
What we wanted to think about, with Water Magic in the context of Umbral Sands' release, was about Water as an element as a whole, powerful, deep, and a source of life.

Water, naturally, is slow to move through and weighs you down - so dealing damage with Water Magic will build up a gradual slowing effect on enemies, making it harder for them to approach. This buildup will peak at 30% reduced movement speed, giving you a noticeable advantage in movement and mobility over a slowed target.

We also wanted to lean into the "healing" aspect of Water, so enemies afflicted with Water magic will have a chance, once you've levelled up enough, to spawn "Water Orbs". These are floating items in the world you can collect, and upon gathering them, they'll restore around a third of your maximum health, over time.
There'll be all the standard fare you expect from magic - combos, special attacks, the works!
We're so excited for you to get your hands on the new Spells and we hope it gives you a better chance of survival out there in the Umbral Sands!
We spoke to Mod Mosey about how we made Water Magic sound crisp and refreshing:

The goal for water magic was to have supporting audio that feels powerful but still sounds full of movement and has the unique timbres associated with water. I started by building a bank of as many different recordings, luckily water has so much to offer, whether it's squeezing a cloth or bubbles underwater or even gurgling some water in my mouth!

The palette ended up being quite large and varied. I then processed them in my digital audio station using techniques like sound morphing (taking two completely different sounds and blending their timbres, pitches and rhythms), reversing the sounds to achieve a "sucking" sound effect for casting and made sure to have a nice blend of my organic water elements with supporting bassy layers that while they aren't necessarily sourced from water recordings they really take the sounds a step further by sweetening it and give the player that desired satisfaction when casting a spell in combat!
We also chatted to the VFX art team to talk about VFX - here's what they had to say:

To create the visual effects for the water spells, we wanted the magic of RuneScape and its world to be reflected in these spells as well, so we decided to create meshes shaped like waves, whirlpools and bubbles.

Once we had the necessary meshes, we created a material which, after some iterations, gave us the look we were after, highlighting the refraction of the water, its colours and, most importantly, adding dynamism to those meshes with internal movement, for which we used vertex movement.

We then put it all together and applied the necessary motion dynamics and synchronisation to adapt the animations and behaviour of the spells within Niagara and Blueprints. In the end, we created water spells that seem imbued with the magic of RuneScape, where the player can feel as though they are controlling the water when using them. We're really happy with the result and we hope players enjoy making a splash with it!

This land was once a thriving civilisation. The Moon Garou, followers of the River Mother, called this home. They built great halls and towers across the land, and found peace here. Fuzan put an end to that.

Sandstone buildings eroded from unnatural sandstorms, and oases dot the landscape of this fraught and corrupted place. The Moon Garou cling to survival in the ruins of their former home, holding back the Kot'Haar. These ancient elemental beings were brought to life in an Age long-forgotten. The fire that bore them has been corrupted and the young dragon Fuzan wreaks havoc with an obsidian army in tow. Kalphites stir from their hives, their glossy carapaces protecting them from the heat as they march to serve their brood. Chitinous, chattering creatures swarm both Dragonkin vaults and Garou ruins.
Garou-ins? Is that anything?

It's not looking great. Thankfully, you aren't stepping into the desert alone. Icthlarin, the Jackal-headed Guardian of Souls and Desert God of the Underworld, is looking to bring order back to this land - and you might just be the ones to help him do it. A fragile peace has been brokered between the distrustful Moon Garou and Icthlarin, and he is hoping to use you as a way to carve a path to Fuzan, and end his reign of terror.
He's just there, at the top of the active volcano. No pressure.
Something New Under The Sun

Sunlight in Umbral Sands is no joke. Stepping into direct sunlight will afflict you with Scorch, a withering effect of Fuzan's corruption that will worsen the longer you are exposed to it. Once triggered, you will rapidly drain Thirst and Hunger - ignore that, and your health is forefeit next.
So, plan your journey. Move from shade to shade, pace yourself and wear protective clothing. Whack a few hasty shelters together, bring a cooling snack or two, and you'll be there in one piece.
At night the air is cool but Fuzan, the Dragon General, brings the heat. With Red Lesser Dragons going to ground, Fuzan attacks from on high - no time of day is safe here.
Gear Up

Adamantite Ore is scattered across the region, offering you increased survivability and the chance to wreak havoc on Dragons, Kalphites and Kot'Haar. You can use the newly raised level caps for Woodcutting and Mining, both of which are now filled up to level 99, to get even more gear stowed away for your team! That's not all - you'll be able to take Red Dragonhide and craft Red Dragonhide ranged armour, and spin cloth to make the tastefully vibrant Infinity Robes! They're as gorgeous as you remember.
Take that gear, and head into the Fight Cave at the base of Fuzan's Tower... the
Fire Cape
is waiting.
The Fight Cave is our take on the iconic challenge from RuneScape - waves of enemies, lava on all sides, and the promise of glory at the end if you make it.

You'll fight stronger Kot'Haar, new mechanics and overcome environmental hazards to earn the right to climb the tower, fight Fuzan and claim a Fire Cape of your own. The Fight Cave is a replayable mode with advanced modes, rare crafting rewards and powerful Vestiges for you to bag.
Exceed Your Limitations
The Fight Cave will shape you, but there is more.
A gateway. A door.

Haunted memories of battles past, powered by Dragonkin conduits across the desert. Enemies reborn - stronger, more unpredictable, more overwhelming. But that is what you must overcome to be greater. The Dragonkin's "Nightmare Crucible" is a test to push you to greatness - because Kuldra will accept nothing less. Your reward for the Nightmare Crucible will be rare materials, allowing you to craft even more "masterful" weapons in the near future.
Unroll A New Ride

Magic Carpets are coming to RuneScape: Dragonwilds as a new mount type in this update. Designed to move you over the dunes - and especially quicksand - safely and swiftly, this new unlock will have you scooting across the sands in no time. We've also gone ahead and added a bunch of new colour variants for your mounts, too!
Architecture and Artistry

We're delighted to be adding an additional set of building pieces for you to sink your teeth into and develop even more masterpieces with - we're excited to see what you create! Your journey through the Umbral Sands will be accompanied by a range of amazing new music tracks for you, including new musicians adding their talents to the score. Firas Zreik lends their talents of the Qanun, Saied Silbak playing the Oud and Hüseyin Kemanci on violin. Amazing talents coming together to blend familiar RuneScape themes with Arabic music from leading world musicians. Lush, richly textured music will run the gamut from loose improvisational solos in the open dunes by day to wonderfully haunting arrangements from dusk until dawn, courtesy of Peter Michael Davidson and our very own Mod Debris. Headphones recommended.
This is our last Major Update before the Scorned Wilderness Raid, the Kuldra boss fight and our full launch onto Steam, EGS, Playstation 5, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch 2 on September 15th.
